ops.reason: architecture changed June 2026 — restarts now route through launchctl kickstart -k, not a direct Popen spawn
ops.content:
The brain daemon restart protocol now routes through `launchctl kickstart -k` rather than a direct Popen spawn. To restart the daemon, invoke:

```
launchctl kickstart -k <service-target>
```

The `-k` flag kills any existing instance before relaunching, ensuring a clean restart. This replaced the previous Popen-based approach as part of the June 2026 architecture change, which brought daemon lifecycle management fully under launchctl supervision.

ops.reason: Architecture changed June 2026: restart flow now routes through launchctl kickstart -k instead of direct Popen spawn.
ops.content: The brain daemon restart protocol now routes through `launchctl kickstart -k` rather than a direct Popen spawn. When a restart is required, the controlling process issues `launchctl kickstart -k gui/<UID>/com.brain.daemon` (or the appropriate service label), which instructs launchd to forcefully stop the current job instance and immediately start a fresh one. This replaces the previous approach of spawning the daemon process directly via Python's `subprocess.Popen`. The launchctl path ensures the daemon inherits the correct launchd environment, respects the plist configuration (including KeepAlive, environment variables, and working directory), and is tracked by launchd for future restarts on failure.

ops.title: WAL checkpoint starvation under parallel sessions
ops.content: When two sessions write concurrently, the TRUNCATE checkpoint starves; symptom is an ever-growing -wal file.
